script.title: संविधान लिखने की फीस पूछी, तो रायज़ादा ने रखी एक शर्त 🤯
script.hook_text: एक पैसा नहीं, बस एक शर्त
sentences: प्रेम बिहारी बोले, संविधान लिखने का एक पैसा नहीं लूँगा।
26 नवंबर 1949 को अपनाए गए संविधान की पहली प्रति उन्होंने हाथ से लिखी थी।
बचपन में माँ-बाप गुज़र गए, तो दादा ने पाला और सुलेख सिखाया।
जवाहरलाल नेहरू ने यह काम सौंपा, तो पूछा गया, कितना लोगे?
जवाब आया, भगवान की कृपा से मेरे पास सब कुछ है।
बस एक शर्त, हर पन्ने पर मेरा नाम, और आख़िरी पन्ने पर दादा का भी।
छह महीने, सैकड़ों निब, और 251 पन्ने, जिनका वज़न 3.75 किलो था।
शर्त मानी गई, दोनों नाम उस प्रति में आज भी दिखते हैं।
जिस दादा ने सुलेख सिखाया, उनका नाम देश के संविधान में है।
script.description:
भारत के संविधान को हाथ से लिखने वाले प्रेम बिहारी नारायण रायज़ादा की कहानी।
फीस में उन्होंने क्या माँगा, जानिए।
claims_en: Prem Behari Narain Raizada said he would not charge a single penny for hand-writing the Constitution.
The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949.
Raizada hand-wrote the first copy of the Constitution.
His parents died when he was young.
He was raised by his grandfather, who taught him calligraphy.
Jawaharlal Nehru asked him to write out the first copy, and he was asked what he would charge.
He replied that by the grace of God he had all things.
His one condition was to write his name on every page and, on the last page, his name with his grandfather's name.
He used hundreds of pen nibs.
The manuscript was 251 pages and weighed 3.75 kg.
The condition was honoured and both names can be seen in the document.
scenes: Extreme close-up of Prem Behari Narain Raizada, a calligrapher in his late 40s with a 1940s Indian look, round spectacles, calm proud half-smile as he politely refuses payment, warm lamplight on his face.
Raizada bent over a large handwritten manuscript page in flowing italic script at a wooden desk in a 1940s Delhi hall, intense focus, soft window light, medium shot, no readable text.

A young boy in 1910s Indian clothes practising calligraphy with a reed pen beside his kindly elderly grandfather in a Persian-style cap, guiding his hand, oil-lamp glow, medium shot, no readable text.
A tall man in a white Gandhi cap and achkan handing a stack of blank parchment to the calligrapher in a 1940s government office, curious expression, daylight, medium shot.
Raizada with hands folded, gentle content smile, shaking his head at an offered envelope, simple 1940s room, soft light, close shot.
Raizada lifting one finger to state his condition, eyes bright and earnest, the blank manuscript pages on the table, warm afternoon light, medium close-up.
A tray of many used steel pen nibs and ink pots beside a thick stack of finished manuscript pages, the calligrapher's hand resting on them, tired satisfied face in the background, lamplight.
Close view of a richly decorated manuscript page with ornate painted borders, a small elegant signature flourish at the corner, Raizada looking at it with quiet pride, no readable letters.
Raizada looking up at a faded framed portrait of his grandfather on the wall, eyes moist, the bound manuscript under his hand, golden evening light, medium close-up.
